supersedes_in_part: The 28 September 2026 adoption of the CR1 subject-clustered t test as the primary paired test (manuscript Methods, Protocol history).
problem: The governing paired test is a cluster-robust t test with a CR1 standard error and G-1 degrees of freedom. With few discordant subjects it is anti-conservative: a comparison with one discordant subject (1 win, 0 losses) gives cluster-t raw p=0.32, where no exact test can give less than 1 (Cameron and Miller 2015, J Hum Resour 50:317-372; MacKinnon and Webb 2018, Econometrics J 21:114-135). The manuscript also labels CR1 'bias-reduced', which describes CR2 (Bell and McCaffrey 2002, Survey Methodology 28:169-181).

rule.governing_test: The exact two-sided subject sign-flip test of the locus-weighted difference (all 2^d assignments for d<=20 nonzero subject aggregates; otherwise 1,000,000 seeded assignments with the plus-one correction; seeds as now) governs every paired development comparison. Holm correction, families and the exclusion of zero-discordance rows from multiplicity are unchanged. A comparison is reported as significant when its sign-flip Holm p < 0.05.
rule.descriptive: The CR1 cluster-t pointwise and Bonferroni-adjusted intervals and p values are kept as descriptive interval estimates of the difference, labelled 'CR1 (finite-cluster-corrected cluster-robust)'. They do not decide significance.
rule.alignment: The confirmatory extension pre-registration already names the exact subject sign-flip test; this makes the development and confirmatory inference use the same test.
rule.label_correction: Every 'CR1 (bias-reduced cluster-robust)' becomes 'CR1 (finite-cluster-corrected cluster-robust)'. This is a factual correction and stands whether or not the governing-test change is signed.

expected_impact_known_before_signature.statement: Not blind. Both tests are already computed for every row (supplementary S3, generated comparison table). The set of comparisons with Holm p < 0.05 is identical under both: RNA-seq ChampHLA-Consensus vs T1K; WES vs HLA-HD, SpecHLA and T1K. No significance conclusion changes; reported p values and the 'Significant' column's basis change. The decision rests on the test's validity with few clusters, not on this effect, and the manuscript must say both.

reporting_commitments: Methods (Endpoints and statistical analysis) names the sign-flip test as governing and the cluster-t as descriptive, with the CR1 label corrected.
Protocol history records this change (9 October 2026) and that it changed no significance conclusion.
S3 and Figure 3 label which test governs; the detectability limits of the discrete sign-flip test are reported in the main text (PSR-013).
